text:
maria: Heads up — noticed a weird mismatch between console token estimates and the reconciled ledger for a streaming request that triggers a tool call and then gets truncated by the client. Console shows ~3.2k provisional tokens, ledger charges ~900. Repro attached below.

jonah: can you paste the raw request / logs? might be a routing vs accounting ordering thing. @sophia fyi in case it's billing semantics.

maria: repro: streaming chat -> model returns chunked tokens, at ~2k tokens we call out to a tool which returns a large JSON, client cancels after receiving the tool result so the stream is truncated. curl for repro:
```bash
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD' -d '{"stream": true, "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"generate long plan and call tool"}]}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/streams
```
And router traces:
```
ROUTER: session=abc123 event=stream_chunk tokens=1984
ROUTER: session=abc123 event=tool_call outbound=true tokens=412
ROUTER: session=abc123 event=client_cancel reason=disconnect
LEDGER: session=abc123 provisional=3200 reconciled=900
```

sophia: this is expected-ish if provisional accounting counts every streamed chunk as provisional and we later roll back the uncommitted prefix when the session truncates. But that large delta is surprising — 3.2k -> 900 seems like double-counting on retries or toolcall attribution.

kevin: on the console side, we're showing "provisional tokens" (what router saw) and "charged tokens" (what ledger settled). UX question: should we surface a third state like "provisionally deducted but reverted" or show a compact cause (e.g., "truncated toolcall"). Right now customers open tickets and get confused.

rachel: router dedupe logic might be failing when the toolcall response contains non-deterministic suffixes. If we dedupe by (session, last_seq) and the client cancelled mid-chunk, the router can emit a partial chunk then a retry which both get counted. We need to check boundary conditions in route-replay.

jonah: quick idea: tag streaming chunks with a session-seq and a "committed" bit set only after EOF or toolcall-return-ack. Ledger only charges committed tokens, console shows provisional until commit window expires. That would require changing the router->ledger event schema.

maria: agree that committed-flag would be cleaner. But we already have provisional attribution for speed. Changing schema during rollout will break older ledger runners unless we have a compatibility path. Also need to handle toolcalls which currently are recorded as separate events with their own token counts.

sophia: billing perspective: minimal change is to add a post-reconcile diff event that emits what was reverted and why. Console can display that and billing can apply credits automatically. That avoids touching the hot path.

kevin: +1 for post-reconcile diff event. We can add a compact UI row: "reconciled adjustments" with hover details listing reasons: truncation, retry-dedupe, toolcall-split. Low-effort and helps support.

rachel: operational note: if we rely on post-reconcile diffs, we should emit telemetry tags to tie back to rollout versions (router image, ledger job id) so we can correlate spikes to deploys.

billing-bot: ledger-reconcile job finished: id=lr-20260317-81 status=complete diffs=23 total_adjustment=-1_234_567 tokens. Link: https://internal.redwood/ledger/lr-20260317-81

maria: thanks — that ledger job id matches the session ids I'm seeing. Can someone run an extraction of sessions that had tool_calls + client_cancel within 5s and list the provisional vs reconciled deltas? would like the distribution.

jonah: I'll run a quick query against the events table tomorrow morning and share a csv. If we see heavy tail, we should prioritize the committed-flag in router events.

kevin: for the rollout UX: plan A: implement post-reconcile diffs + console row (low risk). Plan B: follow up with committed-flag roll out behind a feature flag with a canary in "dedicated" customers. Need feature-flag gating to avoid old ledger runners.

sophia: also add a billing alert when daily reconciled adjustments exceed some pct of provisional. It helps us detect regressions early.

rachel: FYI deploy-bot says we rolled router v3.12.1 two hours before the spike. Could be related.

deploy-bot: deploy: router v3.12.1 -> image sha:sha256:abcd timestamp=2319874000 by @ci-cd 

maria: action items: 1) jonah -> run session extraction and share csv (ETA tomorrow). 2) kevin -> design console "reconciled adjustments" row (low effort) and wire to ledger diffs. 3) sophia -> set provisional vs reconciled alert threshold. 4) rachel -> audit router dedupe boundary conditions in v3.12.1.

jonah: adding: I'll include a small proto change spec if committed-flag looks necessary.

kevin: ping me when the csv is posted, I'll mock the UI with real numbers.

sophia: thanks — cc @support for visibility.

maria: thanks all. I'll drop the first session list into #eng-platform when jonah posts. :thumbsup:
